definitions.explanation: Organized activities aimed at promoting, maintaining, or restoring peace, including diplomacy, education, demonstrations, and humanitarian work.

examples.japanese: ⟦{国連|こくれん}→国連：12035_kokuren⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{平和活動|へいわかつどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}する→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧。
examples.english: To participate in United Nations peace activities.

examples.japanese: ⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{平和活動|へいわかつどう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一環|いっかん}→一環：17696_ikkan⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{折|お}り{鶴|づる}→折り鶴：12782_orizuru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: We made paper cranes at school as part of peace activities.

examples.japanese: ⟦{広島|ひろしま}→広島：28985_hiroshima⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{長崎|ながさき}→長崎：30731_nagasaki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{被爆|ひばく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{経験|けいけん}→経験：01179_keiken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{伝|つた}える→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧{平和活動|へいわかつどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Hiroshima and Nagasaki have continued peace activities for many years to share the experience of the atomic bombings.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧ (peace) and ⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧ (activities). Peace activities hold special significance in Japan due to its postwar pacifist constitution and the experiences of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Schools, civic groups, and local governments regularly organize peace-related events.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平和活動|へいわかつどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{取|と}り{組|く}む→取り組む：04225_torikumu⟧: to engage in peace activities
- {平和活動|へいわかつどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{推進|すいしん}する→推進する：17281_suishinsuru⟧: to promote peace efforts
- {平和活動|へいわかつどう}{家|か}: peace activist
- ⟦{国際|こくさい}→国際：01406_kokusai⟧{平和活動|へいわかつどう}: international peace activities

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{平和運動|へいわうんどう}→平和運動：29187_heiwaundou⟧: peace movement — implies a more organized, political campaign
- PKO (⟦{平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}→平和維持活動：23273_heiwaijikatsudou⟧): peacekeeping operations — specifically military or UN-led missions
- {反戦|はんせん}⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧: anti-war activities — focused specifically on opposing war rather than promoting peace broadly
